title: A Little Too Early to Clap
scene: At a small jazz show, you clap during a pause that turns out not to be the end of the song. Your friend tries to make you feel better, and you learn to wait for the room.
sceneJa: 小さなジャズライブ。曲が終わったと思って拍手したら、実は演奏の途中だった。周囲の視線に気まずくなり、友人の気遣いに救われながら、次は周りの拍手を待つことにする。

questions.question: Which chunking best keeps the expression ‘take it as my cue’ together?
options: The pianist paused / and I took it as my cue / to start clapping.
The pianist / paused and I took it / as my / cue to start clapping.
The pianist paused and / I took it as / my cue to / start clapping.
questions.explanation: ‘Take it as my cue’ means treating something as the signal to act. Keep that expression intact, then add the action.

questions.question: What does ‘play it off as enthusiastic support’ mean in this story?
options: Ask the pianist to start the song again.
Pretend the early applause was a deliberate show of support.
Explain that the audience was too quiet.
questions.explanation: ‘Play it off as ...’ means trying to make an awkward or accidental action seem intentional or harmless.

questions.question: Why does the friend say ‘For what it's worth, I thought it was over too’?
options: To blame the pianist for stopping.
To ask the narrator to clap louder.
To reassure the narrator that the mistake was understandable.
questions.explanation: ‘For what it's worth’ gently offers a thought that may or may not help. Here it makes the narrator feel less embarrassed.

speak: Imagine applauding too early at a live performance. Round 1: Read ‘The pianist paused / and I took it as my cue / to start clapping’ slowly, pausing only at the slashes. Round 2: Stress ‘cue’ and ‘clapping’; then read ‘For what it's worth, / I thought it was over too’ in a warm, quiet voice. Round 3: Read all six sentences with a lightly embarrassed, then amused tone. Speak for 30 seconds: Describe a time you misunderstood a signal. Use ‘I took it as my cue to ...’, ‘I tried to play it off as ...’, and ‘For what it's worth ...’. Final Read: Read the six sentences again without looking at the Japanese.
review: Reuse: Lesson 92 ‘Just to make sure’ (念のため確認する) was used to confirm a meeting entrance; here it means waiting to be certain before clapping. Lesson 90 ‘By the time ...’ (〜するころには) described a change during a football match; today ‘By the end of the night ...’ sets a similar time frame in a music story. New chunks: ‘take it as my cue to ...’ (〜する合図だと受け取る), ‘play it off as ...’ (〜だったことにして取り繕う), and ‘for what it's worth’ (参考になるか分からないけど／慰めになるか分からないけど).
